evidence_packet.lead: Assistant chief fire officer Jim Willmott said he had never seen the control room so hectic
evidence_packet.summary: Assistant chief fire officer Jim Willmott said he had never seen the control room so hectic
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fire chiefs in Greater Manchester have said the service is experiencing its busiest period in decades - as a series of serious blazes broke out at the peak of the recent UK heatwave Crews were already dealing with a large wildfire near Oldham on Wednesday when a semi-detached house also went up in flames in south Manchester the next day A raft of fires across the country, including devastating blazes in the West Midlands, later prompted the government to issue a temporary ban on disposable barbecues Greater Manchester's Chief Fire Officer Dave Russel thanked crews for their work in an "exceptionally busy period" while his deputy Jim Willmott said firefighters had received 1,200 calls on Thursday Willmott told BBC Radio Manchester : "Yesterday I was in the fire control room for North West Fire Control - it really was the most incredibly busy period I have ever seen in my 26 years of service." Earlier in the month crews stood down from wildfires on two stretches of moorland near Dove Stone Reservoir and at Tintwistle and Swineshore

title: Mum-of-three from Bury fears sunbeds caused skin tumour

evidence_packet.title: Mum-of-three from Bury fears sunbeds caused skin tumour
evidence_packet.lead: Justine, 45, is urging people to think carefully before using sunbeds following her diagnosis
evidence_packet.summary: Justine, 45, is urging people to think carefully before using sunbeds following her diagnosis
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother-of-three who used sunbeds in her late teens and early 20s has urged people to think carefully before using them after being diagnosed with a skin tumour Justine Robinson, from Bury, Greater Manchester, said she used the tanners "on and off" before holidays or nights out because she wrongly believed she needed a "base tan" "I can't help wondering whether that's what caused this - it just isn't worth it," said the 45-year-old, who is now recovering after skin cancer surgery Her warning comes after a government consultation on proposals to introduce new safeguards using powers under the Sunbeds Act in England Justine discovered she an uncommon type of melanocytic tumour – which means it cannot be classified as either benign or malignant - after she was referred to a specialist at Salford Royal Hospital It was treated as melanoma as a precaution and she was referred to The Christie for a wider local excision to remove additional tissue around the mole

title: Northenden house blaze causes fireball and 90ft column of smoke

evidence_packet.title: Northenden house blaze causes fireball and 90ft column of smoke
evidence_packet.lead: Neighbours describe seeing the fireball as the blaze began in a conservatory before spreading
evidence_packet.summary: Neighbours describe seeing the fireball as the blaze began in a conservatory before spreading
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Neighbours of a house that was gutted by fire have told of seeing a fireball and a 90ft (about 27m) column of black smoke The fire broke out at the semi-detached property on Norleigh Road, in Northenden, Manchester, at about 14:30 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said five engines and an aerial appliance were sent to tackle the blaze. The house lost a large part of its roof One neighbour said: "I was waiting for a delivery and then saw the fireball." Another neighbour told BBC Radio Manchester: "I have never seen smoke so black before." A GMFRS spokesperson said: "The fire initially broke out in the conservatory of the semi-detached house and spread to the rest of the property "Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus used four hose reels and a thermal imaging camera to extinguish the fire."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tributes to 'legendary' Man Utd fan and podcaster - BBC News Image caption, Darren Webb, right, was a regular on BBC Radio Manchester By Stewart Whittingham North West Published 14 August 2026 Tributes have been paid to a "legendary" Manchester United fan and podcaster who travelled the world to follow the Red Devils. Darren Webb, who ran the Webby & O'Neill podcast, died from cancer on 12 August, his family said. They announced their "devastating loss" with "deep sorrow and unimaginable grief", adding Webb had suffered a "long battle with cancer". Happy Mondays singer Rowetta and Charlatans frontman Tim Burgess were also among those leaving tributes to "Webby". Rowetta said she would him "so much" and thanked him for "always looking out for me". In their statement, his family said: "Darren absolutely loved life, his family, friends, followers and his beloved United." They said they would announce memorial plans "in due course". Tony O'Neill, who co-presented the podcast, said he was "absolutely heartbroken". He added: "We've lost our mate, and that's what hurts the most. "Anyone who knew Webby or watched us over the years knows what he was like. "What you saw was what you got. "He loved United, loved a laugh and could certainly give you his opinion." Image caption, Rowetta said Webby was more than a friend to her and like a brother Tim Burgess described him as "a close friend", adding: "His smile lit up a room and his off-the-record stories about United were a treat to hear." Fellow football fans told of their shock and sadness at Webb's death on social media. Mark Gandy said he was "absolutely gutted" and that he "could listen to Webby telling stories all day long". evidence_packet.summary: Cheshire Police said the investigation spanned 19 counties across England
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Twenty people have been charged in connection with the large-scale theft of plant hire machinery worth about £1m The 14 men and six women were all arrested in 2025 as part of an investigation by Cheshire Police into the theft of equipment - mainly mechanical diggers - from hire companies across the UK The force previously said the investigation involved an alleged conspiracy spanning from September 2020 to February 2025 The allegations involved using false identities in order to hire out plant equipment "with no intent of ever returning the machines," it added The reported thefts took place in Cheshire, Lancashire, Cumbria, Humberside, Hampshire, West Midlands, Hertfordshire, Somerset, Staffordshire, Merseyside, Derbyshire, Greater Manchester, North Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, Suffolk, Cornwall and Lincolnshire The following suspects are set to appear in Chester Magistrates' Court on 9 September

title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas

evidence_packet.title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas
evidence_packet.lead: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
evidence_packet.summary: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town centre by 2040 Bev Craig, who became metro mayor of Greater Manchester in July, said: "I want to carry on and go further with the work of Mayoral Development Corporations across the region "I want to build genuinely affordable homes on publicly owned land and, by getting the private sector to back us, I'm excited about what we can achieve with our MDCs, in places like Ashton-under-Lyne, Stalybridge and Oldham." Mayoral Development Corporations are used to speed up regeneration projects by bringing land, funding, and planning powers together to attract investment They are able to use compulsory purchase powers to make sites available for housing projects and many MDCs are able to grant planning permission for developments

title: Moorland hit by fresh wildfire as heatwave peaks

evidence_packet.title: Moorland hit by fresh wildfire as heatwave peaks
evidence_packet.lead: It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Done Stone Reservoir for weeks
evidence_packet.summary: It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Done Stone Reservoir for weeks
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Firefighters have brought a fresh wildfire in Greater Manchester under control in an area plagued by the blazes all summer Fire crews were sent to the blaze near Holmfirth Road in Oldham, at about 22:25 BST on Wednesday - with the fire covering an area of about 1,640 by 492ft (500m by 150m) at its height Engines remained at the scene on Thursday afternoon dampening down hotspots and working to prevent the fire from spreading It comes just weeks after major wildfires burned across nearby land at Dove Stone Reservoir and Swineshaw for almost three weeks, with a major incident declared The major incident was stood down earlier this month are the fires were largely contained Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said the latest fire was not connected to those earlier blazes and the cause was being investigated

evidence_packet.lead: Bev Craig says planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses built near housing
evidence_packet.summary: Bev Craig says planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses built near housing
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said planning rules should be reviewed after complaints about warehouses being built close to people's homes Speaking on BBC Radio Manchester's Hot Seat , Bev Craig said she agreed with concerns raised by campaigners from the Astley Warehouse Action Group and questioned why modern industrial developments were being allowed closer to residential properties than traditional industry The group was formed after the construction of large warehouses at Astley Business Park near Tyldesley Residents have complained about the scale of the development, its proximity to homes and concerns over noise from future operations During Thursday's programme, campaigner John asked whether residents could continue to rely on mayoral support as they were entering what he described as a new phase of the campaign, focused on the effect the warehouses would have once fully operational Craig said that lessons needed to be learned from the situation

evidence_packet.title: Mum-of-three from Bury fears sunbeds caused skin tumour
evidence_packet.lead: A mother-of-three who used sunbeds in her late teens and early 20s has urged people to think carefully before using them after being diagnosed with a skin tumour Justine Robinson, from Bury, Greater Manchester, said she used the tanners "on and off" before holidays or nights out
evidence_packet.summary: A mother-of-three who used sunbeds in her late teens and early 20s has urged people to think carefully before using them after being diagnosed with a skin tumour Justine Robinson, from Bury, Greater Manchester, said she used the tanners "on and off" before holidays or nights out
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother-of-three who used sunbeds in her late teens and early 20s has urged people to think carefully before using them after being diagnosed with a skin tumour Justine Robinson, from Bury, Greater Manchester, said she used the tanners "on and off" before holidays or nights out because she wrongly believed she needed a "base tan" "I can't help wondering whether that's what caused this - it just isn't worth it," said the 45-year-old, who is now recovering after skin cancer surgery Her warning comes after a government consultation on proposals to introduce new safeguards using powers under the Sunbeds Act in England Justine discovered she an uncommon type of melanocytic tumour – which means it cannot be classified as either benign or malignant - after she was referred to a specialist at Salford Royal Hospital It was treated as melanoma as a precaution and she was referred to The Christie for a wider local excision to remove additional tissue around the mole

evidence_packet.lead: Neighbours of a house that was gutted by fire have told of seeing a fireball and a 90ft (about 27m) column of black smoke The fire broke out at the semi-detached property on Norleigh Road, in Northenden, Manchester, at about 14:30 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Fire and Rescu
evidence_packet.summary: Neighbours of a house that was gutted by fire have told of seeing a fireball and a 90ft (about 27m) column of black smoke The fire broke out at the semi-detached property on Norleigh Road, in Northenden, Manchester, at about 14:30 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Fire and Rescu
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Neighbours of a house that was gutted by fire have told of seeing a fireball and a 90ft (about 27m) column of black smoke The fire broke out at the semi-detached property on Norleigh Road, in Northenden, Manchester, at about 14:30 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said five engines and an aerial appliance were sent to tackle the blaze. The house lost a large part of its roof One neighbour said: "I was waiting for a delivery and then saw the fireball." Another neighbour told BBC Radio Manchester: "I have never seen smoke so black before." A GMFRS spokesperson said: "The fire initially broke out in the conservatory of the semi-detached house and spread to the rest of the property "Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus used four hose reels and a thermal imaging camera to extinguish the fire."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tributes have been paid to a "legendary" Manchester United fan and podcaster who travelled the world to follow the Red Devils Darren Webb, who ran the Webby & O'Neill podcast, died from cancer on 12 August, his family said They announced their "devastating loss" with "deep sorrow and unimaginable grief", adding Webb had suffered a "long battle with cancer" Happy Mondays singer Rowetta and Charlatans frontman Tim Burgess were also among those leaving tributes to "Webby" Rowetta said she would him "so much" and thanked him for "always looking out for me" In their statement, his family said: "Darren absolutely loved life, his family, friends, followers and his beloved United."

evidence_packet.title: Twenty charged over £1m plant hire machinery thefts
evidence_packet.lead: Twenty people have been charged in connection with the large-scale theft of plant hire machinery worth about £1m The 14 men and six women were all arrested in 2025 as part of an investigation by Cheshire Police into the theft of equipment - mainly mechanical diggers - from hire c
evidence_packet.summary: Twenty people have been charged in connection with the large-scale theft of plant hire machinery worth about £1m The 14 men and six women were all arrested in 2025 as part of an investigation by Cheshire Police into the theft of equipment - mainly mechanical diggers - from hire c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Twenty people have been charged in connection with the large-scale theft of plant hire machinery worth about £1m The 14 men and six women were all arrested in 2025 as part of an investigation by Cheshire Police into the theft of equipment - mainly mechanical diggers - from hire companies across the UK The force previously said the investigation involved an alleged conspiracy spanning from September 2020 to February 2025 The allegations involved using false identities in order to hire out plant equipment "with no intent of ever returning the machines," it added The reported thefts took place in Cheshire, Lancashire, Cumbria, Humberside, Hampshire, West Midlands, Hertfordshire, Somerset, Staffordshire, Merseyside, Derbyshire, Greater Manchester, North Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, Suffolk, Cornwall and Lincolnshire The following suspects are set to appear in Chester Magistrates' Court on 9 September

title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas

evidence_packet.title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas
evidence_packet.lead: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town c
evidence_packet.summary: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town centre by 2040 Bev Craig, who became metro mayor of Greater Manchester in July, said: "I want to carry on and go further with the work of Mayoral Development Corporations across the region "I want to build genuinely affordable homes on publicly owned land and, by getting the private sector to back us, I'm excited about what we can achieve with our MDCs, in places like Ashton-under-Lyne, Stalybridge and Oldham." Mayoral Development Corporations are used to speed up regeneration projects by bringing land, funding, and planning powers together to attract investment They are able to use compulsory purchase powers to make sites available for housing projects and many MDCs are able to grant planning permission for developments

At one point, the van could be seen clipping a roundabout and narrowly avoiding a car The driver's luck finally ran out when the van mounted a pedestrian crossing and hit a stationary car. Greater Manchester Police says it received a 999 call at 6.23pm on Wednesday about a van containing parcels worth around £1,000 being stolen in Bolton With the support of the caller, officers located the van within 15 minutes, but the driver made off from police at speed. Specialist GMP Transport Unit officers began to pursue the vehicle, with a chase lasting 40 minutes and crossing into Lancashire GMP says that at times in the pursuit, the van reached speeds exceeding triple the speed limit and damaged multiple pieces of street furniture. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Praying for rain: The farms driven to breaking point Special Report: From heat-stressed cows kept indoors to half-empty crop sheds and emergency winter feeding, local farmers reveal why this summer is like nothing they have seen in Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:00, 15 Aug 2026 On Park Farm in Walmersley, where her family has worked the land since 1957, Margaret Lees is facing a situation unlike anything she has witnessed in over three decades "Everything's running dry basically," says Margaret, who married into the family farm in 1992. "At the moment, we're having to feed the winter silage, feed that is made for the winter, because we’ve not got enough grass "We've always tried to look ahead and make sure that we've got enough silage for every year, but we're feeding this winter's feed now. We've never done this before, as far as I can remember. It’s pretty dire really." Across Greater Manchester and the wider North West, the impact of the UK's driest July on record is driving local agriculture to breaking point View 9 Images Margaret Lees on Park Farm in Walmersley (Image: Park Farm )

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires People who start moor fires should face 'harsher consequences', firefighters say Firefighters have spoken of the difficult conditions they've been dealing with Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 20:07, 14 Aug 2026 View 3 Images The fire on The people responsible for starting moor fires should face "harsher consequences" for their actions, according to the fire crew who have been left to tackle the blazes For more than five weeks, crew from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service have been fighting moor fires at Dovestone, Swineshaw and now Saddleworth The crew who have been working tirelessly in "very, very difficult" conditions to stop the fires from spreading say that people responsible for starting them should be given more serious consequences to help stop this from happening in the future It comes as firefighters remain at the scene of a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road (A635) in Saddleworth, where crews continue to work in challenging conditions to contain the incident and dampen down affected areas Since the fire was first reported on Wednesday evening, around 50 firefighters have been working alongside landowners and the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) to bring the fire under control in extremely high temperatures

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Man, 64, was seen on busy Rochdale street 10 days ago then disappeared An urgent appeal has been issued to find James News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:25, 14 Aug 2026 View Image James is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a missing Rochdale man who was last seen 10 days ago. Officers are searching for James The 64-year-old was last seen on Albert Royds Street, in Rochdale, at midday on Tuesday, August 4. Greater Manchester Police has issued an appeal to find him on social media this afternoon (August 14) James is described as being white, around 5ft 6ins tall, of slim build and with dark hair. He usually wears skinny jeans and occasionally wears a bobble hat, according to GMP. Anyone with information that could assist GMP is being urged to come forward A GMP Rochdale spokesperson said: "Can you help police find missing James? James was last seen on Albert Royds Street in Rochdale at around 12pm on August 4, 2026 "Officers are becoming increasingly concerned for James' welfare and want to ensure he is safe and well. Anyone with information about James' whereabouts is asked to contact police on 0161 856 8643, quoting MSP/06PP/0001307/26."

evidence_packet.title: Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured The pursuit came to a sudden stop at a pedestrian crossing News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:21, 14 Aug 2026 View Image The moment a man runs to safety while Racing at dangerous speeds, f
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured The pursuit came to a sudden stop at a pedestrian crossing News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:21, 14 Aug 2026 View Image The moment a man runs to safety while Racing at dangerous speeds, f
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured The pursuit came to a sudden stop at a pedestrian crossing News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:21, 14 Aug 2026 View Image The moment a man runs to safety while Racing at dangerous speeds, failing to hit the brakes at red traffic lights and forcing a pedestrian to run for safety - this was the reckless moment the driver of a stolen van tried to evade police The vehicle reached speeds of up to 100mph during a pursuit through Bolton, Wigan and Chorley on Wednesday (August 14). At one point, the van could be seen clipping a roundabout and narrowly avoiding a car The driver's luck finally ran out when the van mounted a pedestrian crossing and hit a stationary car. Greater Manchester Police says it received a 999 call at 6.23pm on Wednesday about a van containing parcels worth around £1,000 being stolen in Bolton With the support of the caller, officers located the van within 15 minutes, but the driver made off from police at speed. Specialist GMP Transport Unit officers began to pursue the vehicle, with a chase lasting 40 minutes and crossing into Lancashire GMP says that at times in the pursuit, the van reached speeds exceeding triple the speed limit and damaged multiple pieces of street furniture. A cyclist was also injured by the van, though thankfully their injuries were not serious, according to police

This type of concrete is prone to sudden unexpected collapse The school later reopened after safety measures were put in place and all classrooms in the school are now open. evidence_packet.lead: Manchester weather Praying for rain: The farms driven to breaking point Special Report: From heat-stressed cows kept indoors to half-empty crop sheds and emergency winter feeding, local farmers reveal why this summer is like nothing they have seen in Comments News Charlotte Fishe
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester weather Praying for rain: The farms driven to breaking point Special Report: From heat-stressed cows kept indoors to half-empty crop sheds and emergency winter feeding, local farmers reveal why this summer is like nothing they have seen in Comments News Charlotte Fishe
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather Praying for rain: The farms driven to breaking point Special Report: From heat-stressed cows kept indoors to half-empty crop sheds and emergency winter feeding, local farmers reveal why this summer is like nothing they have seen in Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:00, 15 Aug 2026 On Park Farm in Walmersley, where her family has worked the land since 1957, Margaret Lees is facing a situation unlike anything she has witnessed in over three decades "Everything's running dry basically," says Margaret, who married into the family farm in 1992. "At the moment, we're having to feed the winter silage, feed that is made for the winter, because we’ve not got enough grass "We've always tried to look ahead and make sure that we've got enough silage for every year, but we're feeding this winter's feed now. We've never done this before, as far as I can remember. It’s pretty dire really." Across Greater Manchester and the wider North West, the impact of the UK's driest July on record is driving local agriculture to breaking point View 9 Images Margaret Lees on Park Farm in Walmersley (Image: Park Farm )

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires People who start moor fires should face 'harsher consequences', firefighters say Firefighters have spoken of the difficult conditions they've been dealing with Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 20:07, 14 Aug 2026 View 3 Images The fire on The people responsible for starting moor fires should face "harsher consequences" for their actions, according to the fire crew who have been left to tackle the blazes For more than five weeks, crew from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service have been fighting moor fires at Dovestone, Swineshaw and now Saddleworth The crew who have been working tirelessly in "very, very difficult" conditions to stop the fires from spreading say that people responsible for starting them should be given more serious consequences to help stop this from happening in the future It comes as firefighters remain at the scene of a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road (A635) in Saddleworth, where crews continue to work in challenging conditions to contain the incident and dampen down affected areas Since the fire was first reported on Wednesday evening, around 50 firefighters have been working alongside landowners and the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) to bring the fire under control in extremely high temperatures

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health 'I need to get through this': Dad given incurable diagnosis hopes to walk daughter down the aisle Jason Walker was given a 'shock' diagnosis after suffering two main symptoms Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 17:44, 14 A Lancashire dad battling an incurable blood cancer hopes to be well enough to walk his daughter down the aisle at her wedding after becoming the first patient to take part in a potentially game-changing clinical trial Jason Walker, 57, is determined to beat cancer for a second time ahead of his daughter Abbey's wedding in Montenegro next May. He has been living with the disease for more than a decade after he was diagnosed with stage 3 multiple myeloma in 2014, aged just 45 Jason, from Longridge near Preston, said the initial diagnosis came as a "huge shock" as he was living an active lifestyle. He was diagnosed after suffering persistent back pain and double vision Tests revealed multiple myeloma had spread throughout his body, causing chronic bone pain, particularly around his pelvis. The cancer had also affected the area around his pituitary gland and was pulling on his optic nerve Doctors told him the disease was incurable and that treatment would focus on achieving long-term remission and extending his life

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Man, 64, was seen on busy Rochdale street 10 days ago then disappeared An urgent appeal has been issued to find James News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:25, 14 Aug 2026 View Image James is missing from home (Image: GMP) People are being urged to look out for a missing Rochdale man who was last seen 10 days ago. Officers are searching for James The 64-year-old was last seen on Albert Royds Street, in Rochdale, at midday on Tuesday, August 4. Greater Manchester Police has issued an appeal to find him on social media this afternoon (August 14) James is described as being white, around 5ft 6ins tall, of slim build and with dark hair. He usually wears skinny jeans and occasionally wears a bobble hat, according to GMP. Anyone with information that could assist GMP is being urged to come forward A GMP Rochdale spokesperson said: "Can you help police find missing James? James was last seen on Albert Royds Street in Rochdale at around 12pm on August 4, 2026 "Officers are becoming increasingly concerned for James' welfare and want to ensure he is safe and well. Anyone with information about James' whereabouts is asked to contact police on 0161 856 8643, quoting MSP/06PP/0001307/26."

evidence_packet.title: Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured The pursuit came to a sudden stop at a pedestrian crossing News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:21, 14 Aug 2026 View Image The moment a man runs to safety while Racing at dangerous speeds, f
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured The pursuit came to a sudden stop at a pedestrian crossing News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:21, 14 Aug 2026 View Image The moment a man runs to safety while Racing at dangerous speeds, f
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Stolen van's reckless 100mph attempt to escape police that left cyclist injured The pursuit came to a sudden stop at a pedestrian crossing News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:21, 14 Aug 2026 View Image The moment a man runs to safety while Racing at dangerous speeds, failing to hit the brakes at red traffic lights and forcing a pedestrian to run for safety - this was the reckless moment the driver of a stolen van tried to evade police The vehicle reached speeds of up to 100mph during a pursuit through Bolton, Wigan and Chorley on Wednesday (August 14). At one point, the van could be seen clipping a roundabout and narrowly avoiding a car The driver's luck finally ran out when the van mounted a pedestrian crossing and hit a stationary car. Greater Manchester Police says it received a 999 call at 6.23pm on Wednesday about a van containing parcels worth around £1,000 being stolen in Bolton With the support of the caller, officers located the van within 15 minutes, but the driver made off from police at speed. Specialist GMP Transport Unit officers began to pursue the vehicle, with a chase lasting 40 minutes and crossing into Lancashire GMP says that at times in the pursuit, the van reached speeds exceeding triple the speed limit and damaged multiple pieces of street furniture. A cyclist was also injured by the van, though thankfully their injuries were not serious, according to police

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Most people in the UK already monitor their own health and wellbeing, and an overwhelming majority would be happy to do more if advised by the NHS, according to a new University of Manchester led study In a survey of 4,270 adults from across the UK, the researchers found that 79% had already used some form of self-monitoring, ranging from tracking blood pressure and blood sugar to monitoring fitness, diet, eyesight, hearing and mental wellbeing Published in the journal Archives of Public Health, the findings suggest self-monitoring could play a major role in helping people spot health problems earlier and take greater control of their wellbeing The study was part-funded by a National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Senior Investigator award to lead researcher Professor Kevin Munro and was supported by the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre: Manchester’s Hearing Health Theme The results chime with the Governments aspirations for health monitoring technologies to be part of routine care to support proactive health monitoring and preventative action The study also found that 86% of respondents would be willing to monitor at least one aspect of their health if recommended by the NHS

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The first additional places are expected from September 2027 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has completed the purchase of the former Loreto Preparatory School site on Dunham Road - ending years of uncertainty over the three-acre plot and securing it for the expansion of neighbouring North Cestrian School The acquisition, funded by a Department for Education capital grant, will allow North Cestrian to add up to 300 secondary school places A feasibility study is now underway, with the first additional places expected from September 2027 and the full expansion complete by September 2028 The deal was struck by Trafford's Development and Education teams working alongside Hamblin Education Trust, which runs North Cestrian It draws a line under a two-year campaign that began when Loreto Prep - an independent Catholic primary school with a 114-year history - unexpectedly closed in July 2023 , citing declining pupil numbers and financial pressures

title: "A devastating outcome": Trafford children's services rated 'inadequate' as Ofsted warns children left at risk of harm

evidence_packet.title: "A devastating outcome": Trafford children's services rated 'inadequate' as Ofsted warns children left at risk of harm
evidence_packet.lead: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-we
evidence_packet.summary: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-we
evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-week inspection between June 8th and 19th, judged both the impact of leaders on social work practice and the experiences of children who need help and protection to be inadequate - the watchdog's lowest grade Services for children in care were rated good, while support for care leavers requires improvement to be good Inspectors, led by His Majesty's Inspector Leanne Cooper, found that since the council's last full inspection in 2022 - when it was rated requires improvement across the board - leaders had failed to recognise and act on shortfalls in critical parts of the service The sharpest criticism was reserved for the council's "front door" - the point at which concerns about children are first reported. The report found that responses to contacts about children take too long, are not prioritised in line with risk, and that many children face lengthy Strategy discussions - urgent multi-agency meetings held when a child is identified as being at risk of significant harm - are too often delayed, leaving children in potentially unsafe situations for too long and at risk of what inspectors called unassessed significant harm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crews were already dealing with a large wildfire near Oldham on Wednesday when a semi-detached house also went up in flames in south Manchester the next day A raft of fires across the country, including devastating blazes in the West Midlands, later prompted the government to issue a temporary ban on disposable barbecues Greater Manchester's Chief Fire Officer Dave Russel thanked crews for their work in an "exceptionally busy period" while his deputy Jim Willmott said firefighters had received 1,200 calls on Thursday Willmott told BBC Radio Manchester : "Yesterday I was in the fire control room for North West Fire Control - it really was the most incredibly busy period I have ever seen in my 26 years of service." evidence_packet.evidence_text: The fire broke out at the semi-detached property on Norleigh Road, in Northenden, Manchester, at about 14:30 BST on Thursday Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said five engines and an aerial appliance were sent to tackle the blaze. The house lost a large part of its roof One neighbour said: "I was waiting for a delivery and then saw the fireball." Another neighbour told BBC Radio Manchester: "I have never seen smoke so black before." A GMFRS spokesperson said: "The fire initially broke out in the conservatory of the semi-detached house and spread to the rest of the property "Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus used four hose reels and a thermal imaging camera to extinguish the fire." evidence_packet.summary: Phantom The Lounge on Maclure Road, Rochdale, has received a closure order due to excessive levels of carbon monoxide (CO) found on site by Rochdale Borough Council’s environmental health service
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Phantom The Lounge on Maclure Road, Rochdale, has received a closure order due to excessive levels of carbon monoxide (CO) found on site by Rochdale Borough Council’s environmental health service The closure order was granted at Manchester Magistrates’ Court on 24 July 2026 with evidence given by council environmental health officers, alongside support from officers from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) and Greater Manchester Police (GMP) This follows several routine inspections by environmental health officers, which found that Phantom The Lounge had been illegally operating due to smoking taking place on site in a substantially enclosed area. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

title: Maresca fitness update on McAidoo, Haaland and Rodri

evidence_packet.title: Maresca fitness update on McAidoo, Haaland and Rodri
evidence_packet.lead: Maresca fitness update on McAidoo, Haaland and Rodri
evidence_packet.summary: But the new City boss says that he needs to consider that many of his squad have only just returned after being given time off after playing in the World Cup. The Italian will have the opportunity to fight for his first trophy since taking charge when we face the Gunners at the P
evidence_packet.evidence_text: But the new City boss says that he needs to consider that many of his squad have only just returned after being given time off after playing in the World Cup. The Italian will have the opportunity to fight for his first trophy since taking charge when we face the Gunners at the Principality Stadium for the 15:00 (UK) kick-off. Players that reached the quarter-finals or beyond missed our pre-season tour to Asia, which could potentially impact team selection for the game. Of those that did travel to Hong Kong and South Korea, winger Ryan McAidoo is the only player to suffer a setback, picking up a slight shoulder issue from the first game against Inter. “The only one is Ryan McAidoo who in pre-season had a small problem but he has already worked with us,” Maresca said at his pre-match news conference. “So everyone is fit knowing that some of them just arrived two days ago.” Fans got an opportunity to see the players at our City Are Back open training session at the Joie Stadium earlier this week. Erling Haaland sat out some of the training but Maresca says he is fine for the start of the season. “Yes he was okay,” he added. “He just had some small things behind his heels but he’s okay.” Maresca confirmed that Rodri is back at the CFA after successful minor back surgery following the World Cup. “He’s now in rehab,” the boss added. “When he’s ready to start training session with us, this is the problem for him.” Premier League 2026/27 home tickets now on sale General admission tickets for Manchester City’s home 2026/27 Premier League fixtures are now on sale to Premium, Matchday and Junior Members.
